$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.grammar.json. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-JSON-ROOT-UNTIGHTENED
arms.note: the root value keeps the span the parser gives it, which starts at offset 0 over the document's leading whitespace, so the writer finds no delimiter at the root's first byte

arms.name: M-JSON-DIRTY-NEVER
arms.note: no gap counts as touched by an edit, so an appended entry keeps the raw ` ` after its `,` and a deletion leaves the doubled space it closed up

arms.name: M-JSON-TOUCH-IGNORED
arms.find: || ((mark.from == mark.to || gap.from == gap.to) && mark.from <= gap.to && gap.from <= mark.to)
arms.note: only an OVERLAPPING mark touches a gap: the empty gaps around the first entry of an empty container are never re-derived, so it stays `["x"]` under an expanded parent

arms.name: M-JSON-NOTHING-NEW
arms.note: no node counts as introduced by an edit, so a new object is written as an existing one with every gap touched — inline, whatever its sibling's shape

arms.name: M-JSON-STYLE-ALWAYS-EXPANDED
arms.note: every touched container is laid out one entry per line, so an entry appended to an inline array breaks it open

arms.name: M-JSON-EMPTY-INLINE
arms.note: a container with no untouched gap is inline instead of following its parent, so the first entry of an empty array under an expanded object stays on the array's line

arms.name: M-JSON-NEW-MODEL-IGNORED
arms.find: final shaped: Null<QueryNode> = model != null && model.kind == node.kind && model.children.length > 0 ? model : null;
arms.note: a new container never looks at its nearest sibling, so a new object beside an inline one comes out expanded

arms.name: M-JSON-KEYSEP-DEFAULT
arms.note: a new member's `:` always takes the default spacing, so a document written `"a" : 1` gains a `"b": 2`

arms.name: M-JSON-INDENT-DEFAULT
arms.note: the indent unit is always a tab, so a line an edit adds to a two-space document is indented by a tab

arms.name: M-JSON-LINE-END-LF
arms.note: every line an edit adds ends in LF, so a CRLF document gains mixed line ends

arms.name: M-JSON-MARKS-UNSHIFTED
arms.note: each edit's footprint is placed at its offset in the ORIGINAL document, so a second insert's mark misses the entry it introduced

arms.name: M-JSON-LITERAL-NONE
arms.note: no JSON string reads as a literal, so `--sorted` refuses every JSON array as holding no constant strings

arms.name: M-JSON-REGIONS-NONE
arms.note: the JSON grammar reports no string region, so every byte of a key or a string value reads as code

arms.name: M-JSON-PATTERN-NO-METAVAR
arms.note: a `"$x"` string in a pattern stays a string, so a JSON pattern can hold no metavariable

arms.name: M-JSON-VALUE-RAW
arms.note: a JSON string sorts by its raw spelling, so an escape sorts apart from the character it spells

arms.name: M-JSON-QUOTE-LONE-SURROGATE
arms.note: a string is quoted with nothing escaped: a lone surrogate is written bare, and UTF-8 output turns it into a different character

arms.name: M-JVALUE-FIELD-NULL-HELD
arms.note: a key holding null reads as a held value, unlike every schema reader of the same document

arms.name: M-NATIVE-COMPACT-NEVER
arms.note: the compact options go to the Doc writer, which spells a space after every comma

arms.name: M-JVALUE-AT-LOOSE-INDEX
arms.find: index == null || '$index' != segment || index < 0 || index >= items.length
arms.note: an index is whatever number a segment starts with, so `1x` and `01` both read element 1 instead of nothing
